Wisdom of Solomon 2 lets you hear the synagogue of Satan think. “For the ungodly said, reasoning with themselves, but not aright, Our life is short and tedious, and in the death of a man there is no remedy: neither was there any man known to have returned from the grave.” This ungodly is Esau.

Now watch what Esau says about us. “He was made to reprove our thoughts.” The Israelite man, the prophet, was made to reprove their thoughts. “He is grievous unto us even to behold”: just looking at us grieves them, because we are a constant reminder that we are the sons of God and they are not. “For his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion”, because we keep the commandments of God.

“We are esteemed of him as counterfeits”. That goes to Revelation 2:9 and 3:9: they are counterfeits, fakes, frauds; they are not the real Jews. The Bible calls them counterfeits; those are not my words, those are the words of God. “He abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed”.

So those which say they are Jews and are not know it themselves. The righteous man grieves them, and that is why the devil casts some of us into prison. Be faithful unto death.

precepts.text: God created man to be immortal and made him an image of his own eternity.
precepts.point: 'Replenish' means to fill again, and Adam was told to subdue the earth.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
What does it mean when the Lord says, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness”? Wisdom of Solomon 2:23: “For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.” That is how Adam was created before he sinned: immortal. Being in God's image is not only about how we look. It goes into his power and his divinity too.

2 Esdras 8:44 says man “is called thine own image, because thou art like unto him, for whose sake thou hast made all things”. Adam was just like his father, the way someone says, you are just like your father, you are the image of your father. We are supposed to be in the image of Christ, and Christ is in the image of the Father. All things were created for Adam and for the sons of Adam, which is us. Not everyone was created in Adam's image; the sons of God are the ones created in Adam's image, because Adam was created in God's image.

“and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth”. That is the kingdom of Adam, in so many words. Then in verse 28 God tells them, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it”. To replenish means to fill something up again. There is a big gap after verse 27: a lot of time went by. Why would God tell Adam to subdue the earth if he already had dominion over it? That was left to be answered later in the class.

Deuteronomy 11:21 shows Moses saw Adam's kingdom: keep the commandments in the land, and your days will be “as the days of heaven upon the earth.” The kingdom of heaven was once on the earth, when Adam ruled. 2 Esdras 7:26 speaks of the bride that “now is withdrawn from the earth”: that holy city, the access to the spirit realm, withdrew itself from the earth, so it must once have been on the earth, in the time of Adam. How Adam was on the earth is how we are going to be in the future.

precepts.text: Through envy of the devil came death into the world.
precepts.point: His boughs, Israel, were delivered to death in the nether parts of the earth, and the nations shook at his fall.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
The great cedar was so fair that “all the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied him.” The fir trees were not like his boughs, the chesnut trees not like his branches. His boughs and branches were his true children, his firstborn in the heavens, immortal and ruling with him. The other trees were the children Adam had on the earth before the fall, not created in his image, the multitude “born in vain.” They envied him, and they envied the twelve tribes that were with him.

Wisdom of Solomon shows who else envied him: “For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity. Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world.” The man God created was Adam. Adam was immortal and his sons were immortal; the children he had on the earth were created as men, sons of men, and were not immortal.

The devil also envied Adam. Satan went to war with Adam, and when he could not get him, he went through his woman to take him down: he jumped on his wife, played with her emotions and tricked her. Through the envy of Satan, that is how death came.

It will be the same in the future: “The heathen shall envy thee, but they shall be able to do nothing against thee.” When Christ returns and sets us back on this earth to rule, the nations will envy us, the same as back then, but they will not be able to do anything against us.

precepts.point: That attitude toward a just man was written down long before.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“My Father worketh hitherto, and I work.” They sought the more to kill him, because he “said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God.” That attitude toward a just man was written down long before.

Solomon gives the words of the wicked against the just: “We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and maketh his boast that God is his father.”

He maketh his boast that God is his father. That is the very thing the Jews held against Christ: he said God was his Father. And he abstained from their ways as from filthiness, and esteemed them as counterfeits. Their hatred of him was foretold word for word.

This is what King David prophesied about when he said he was afraid of the enemies that compassed him about.

“Let us oppress the poor righteous man”: this is what those that say they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan, will say. “Let us not spare the widow, nor reverence the ancient gray hairs”: this man, this devil, is not going to care how young you are, how old you are; if you’re a woman, he don’t give a damn.

“Let our strength be the law of justice”: that’s why they always send their kids to be judges, lawyers, all in the court system. When we go for representation, these so-called Jewish lawyers say we’re not allowed to represent Israel United in Christ; we’ve had several cases of that. Then we go to the black ones: I’m not sure if I can do that, because they’re afraid of these people. Y’all don’t know what we go through; we just keep it quiet. “For that which is feeble is found to be nothing worth”: we’re the people, we’re the ones found to be nothing worth.

“Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous”: so this devil, this white man, says. “Because he is not for our turn”: no, we’re not for their turn. “And he is clean contrary to our doings”: we’re opposites, everything that they do. “He upbraideth us with our offending the law”: because they say they believe in the Bible, but they break every Torah law there is. “And objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education”: their education is based on the Talmud, on the Kabbalah. That’s not Bible; that has nothing to do with the Most High.

“He professeth to have the knowledge of God”: which we do. “And he calleth himself the child of the Lord”: God calls us the children of God; didn’t he say Israel is my son, even my firstborn? We’re God’s children. “He was made to reprove our thoughts”: that’s why we were made. “He is grievous unto us even to behold”: he can’t stand to look at us. “His ways are of another fashion.”

“We are esteemed of him as counterfeits”: phonies, frauds, fakes. Y’all see what the Bible is saying? They are counterfeits; they’re not the Jews the Bible speaks of. “He pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed”: that’s why we tell you, brothers, don’t worry about your end; your end shall be blessed. Sisters, your end shall be blessed.

“Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture”: that’s what we read in Revelation 2, that’s the war in Revelation 12:17, that’s what Christ was talking about in Matthew 24:9-10. These are the various precepts of the same thing, letting you know what’s going to happen. “Let us condemn him with a shameful death”: remember it said in Revelation 2, be thou faithful unto death. Solomon is prophesying the same thing.

“Such things they did imagine”: such things this white man did imagine, “and were deceived: for their own wickedness hath blinded them.” “As for the mysteries of God, they knew them not”: they don’t know this Bible. We know the Bible; that’s why they will not sit down with us. They don’t know the scriptures like we know the scriptures. “Neither hoped they for the wages of righteousness, nor discerned a reward for blameless souls.”
